fact: The Registre Social Unique database holds 362,698 households (2,217,518 people) across 99 communes in 10 regions, per the Ministry of Humanitarian Action's representative.

The World Bank says the earlier Burkina Naong Sa Ya project helped establish a national social registry of vulnerable households, a platform for expanding and targeting social protection programs, and the new project will support its expanded coverage and use.
The World Bank SASPP page says the social registry held 344,400 poor households as of June 2025, with roll-out continuing after the safety-net project closed.
The World Bank's PPSAS page says the new PARPS project (approved June 2026) includes the continued roll-out ("poursuite du déploiement") of the Registre social unique (RSU).
